::: {.hero}
## Computational Models in Health Behavior

A curated, open evidence synthesis database for formal computational modeling approaches in health psychology — with a focus on **theory-derived architecture selection** and **just-in-time adaptive interventions**.
:::

### What is this database?

Health behavior research is increasingly using formal computational models — cybernetic control equations, dual-process logistic models, reinforcement learning frameworks, hidden Markov models — to represent behavioral mechanisms. Yet which architecture to use for which behavior is rarely derived from theory in a principled way.

This database tracks published computational models of momentary health behavior and codes them on **three questions** the field currently cannot answer systematically:

1. **Was the architecture theory-derived?** (or chosen by convention/software availability)
2. **Was a cross-architecture comparison conducted?** (a missing standard in current practice)
3. **Were JITAI predictions derived from the fitted model?** (the application layer)

### How entries are structured

Each entry captures one study × behavior combination. The coding scheme maps onto the theory-architecture framework introduced in:

> Jones, C. M. (2025). *A principled framework for selecting and formalizing computational models of momentary behavior: Two illustrative demonstrations grounded in self-regulation theory.* Perspectives on Psychological Science.

Key columns are:

| Column | What it captures |
|---|---|
| Theory group | Which major theory group the authors invoke |
| Architecture | Formal model type selected |
| Mechanism-derived? | Was selection principled from theory (Yes / Partial / No) |
| Cross-arch. validation? | Was a competing architecture tested? |
| ΔELPD | LOO-CV advantage of selected model (if reported) |
| JITAI derived? | Were intervention timing/targeting predictions made? |

### How to contribute

Use the [Submit a Study](submit.qmd) page to propose an entry. Submissions are reviewed before appearing in the verified database. You can also open a GitHub issue or pull request on the [repository](https://github.com/).

### How to cite

If you use data from this database, please cite both the database and the framework paper:

> Jones, C. M. (2026). *Computational Models in Health Behavior — Evidence Synthesis Database* [Data set]. https://[url]

> Jones, C. M. (2025). *A principled framework for selecting and formalizing computational models of momentary behavior.* Perspectives on Psychological Science.
